title: What a model registry tracks
description: A model registry records for every served model: the model ID and revision, which server binary and version runs it, the endpoint URL, the GPU(s) it occupies, its quantization, and its health status. This turns a pile of terminal windows running servers into an inventory you can query. The registry is the difference between 'some servers somewhere' and an organized fleet.

title: vLLM server entries
description: Each vLLM instance registers with its flags (tensor parallel size, max model len, quantization) so the registry knows its capacity and limits. Re-registering on restart keeps the inventory truthful, and stale entries age out via heartbeats. Capacity-aware routing starts with honest registration.

title: TGI server entries
description: Hugging Face Text Generation Inference servers register the same way: model ID, revision, dtype/quantization, and endpoint. TGI's own /info and /health endpoints feed the registry's liveness data. Supporting both vLLM and TGI in one registry avoids running two inventories.

title: Endpoint routing and load balancing
description: With several servers registered, a router spreads chat requests across healthy endpoints: round-robin for even load, least-loaded for bursty traffic, or model-affinity routing that pins a conversation to the server already holding its KV cache warmth. Routing policy is configuration, not code changes.

title: Health checks and failover
description: The registry polls each endpoint's health; a failing server is pulled from rotation and its in-flight requests retried on a healthy replica. Heartbeat timeouts catch hung processes that still hold a port. Failover turns one crashed server from an outage into a log line.

title: Model versioning and revisions
description: Registry entries pin exact model revisions (commit hashes), so 'llama-3-8b' means the same weights everywhere and rollbacks are one pointer change. Canary entries route a slice of traffic to the new revision while metrics are watched. Version pins are how teams stop debugging phantom weight differences.

title: GPU inventory and placement
description: The registry's GPU map shows which cards host which models and how much VRAM each reservation holds, so placing a new model is a lookup instead of nvidia-smi archaeology. Placement rules (keep 70B models off the 24GB cards) are enforced at registration time.

description: One gateway URL fronts all registered servers with the OpenAI chat-completions shape; the model field in the request selects the registry entry. Clients need one base URL forever, while servers come and go behind it. This is the operational payoff of the registry.

title: Metrics per endpoint
description: Per-endpoint metrics (requests/sec, tokens/sec, queue depth, p99 latency, error rate) are scraped into the registry dashboard, making slow or sick servers visible before users complain. Alerts fire on error-rate spikes or queue saturation. Observability is what makes a fleet manageable.

title: Access control and API keys
description: The gateway issues per-client API keys with rate limits and per-model permissions, so the intern's script cannot burn the 70B endpoint. Keys rotate without restarting servers because auth lives at the gateway. Multi-user serving needs this on day one, not day ninety.

title: Cold-start and warm pools
description: Models not currently loaded register as cold with their load cost (weights size, load time); the registry keeps hot pools for popular models and loads cold ones on demand with a 'warming up' response. Placement policy decides what stays hot. This balances VRAM cost against latency.

title: Multi-node serving
description: Registries span machines: agents on each GPU host register local servers with a central control plane over TLS. The control plane never touches weights, only metadata and routing. Scaling past one box is an agent install, not a redesign.

title: Audit log of every change
description: Every registration, routing change, and key rotation is appended to an audit log with who and when. When something breaks at 2am, the log shows the last five changes instead of a mystery. Auditing is cheap and saves incidents.

title: Backup and disaster recovery
description: Registry state (fleet YAML + audit log) backs up to object storage on a schedule; rebuilding the control plane is a restore plus agent reconnect. Model weights themselves are re-pulled from pinned revisions. Recovery time is measured in minutes because state is small and declarative.
